messages.text: What should I understand about phase versus polarity, and when does it matter in a mix?

Ask only context that changes the decision, then present one reversible stereo/mono experiment: Blend the two related signals at matched level, toggle polarity on one, then compare both settings in stereo and mono without moving any timing.
That is more focused and translates better in mono, but it feels a little smaller in stereo.
Reference the exact prior experiment, treat the user report as evidence, and adapt one hypothesis without restarting from generic panning or phase advice.
Why does that result make sense, and what should I learn from it?

Explain the causal principle in plain language and connect it to the exact A/B: Polarity inversion flips the entire waveform vertically; phase describes a frequency-dependent time relationship between signals. A polarity flip can improve one blend but is not a universal phase-alignment command.
